correctness.rationale: For n>=17 the triangles are the quotient of the triangular lattice by L_n={(a,b):a+3b=0 (mod n)}, with H1=L_n and basis u=(-3,1),v=(n,0). The exact step norm is N=max(|a|,|b|,|a-b|). For any nonzero closed edge walk of length ell<=4, |a+3b|<=4ell<=16<n, hence a+3b=0 as an integer and (a,b)=tu. The norm N(tu)=4|t| excludes essential loops of length <4 and forces endpoints +/-u at length4. A word realizing -u in 4 steps must consist of three -e1 and one e2 step; its projections are exactly the n distinct consecutive four-cycles C_i, all primitive. For classes outside Zu, |a+3b|>=n and <=4N<=4ell, giving ell>=ceil(n/4). For n=4r+s the four explicit endpoints (r,r),(r+1,r),(r-1,r+1),(r,r+1) respectively have a+3b=n and N=ceil(n/4); monotone step words of 4s plus at most two final 1/3-steps have no repeated cyclic vertices. The conclusion is unbounded in n; bounded independent checks are corroboration only.

value.rationale: The natural combinatorial edge homology systole on a published vertex-transitive torus triangulation has a complete first carrier shell and two exact independent minima for an infinite parameter family. All n shortest essential cycles lie in a single primitive direction while the next independent minimum grows ceil(n/4), yielding an explicit unbounded rank-two anisotropy ratio. The threshold n>=17 is mathematically meaningful (n=16 admits an extra independent 4-edge +4-step cycle); this is neither a finite isolated datum nor a generic graph-theory exercise, despite the elementary lattice proof. No stronger global metric or torus-optimality statement is claimed.
